automations.name: Lead intake and scoring
automations.what: Checks each website form, matches it to one of the four practice areas, checks the other side against the firm's conflict list, flags court dates and other time-sensitive wording, scores the lead from 0 to 100 and decides the next step. No AI model: every decision is a rule you can read.
automations.evidence: 48 invented leads, 48 of 48 match their labels on area, next step, tier, urgency, conflict result and score. The labels were written before the code and the set never failed, so it did not tune anything.
automations.limit: Written and checked by the same person, so it is a regression set, not an independent test. The conflict check is a screen against a demo list of 22 invented names.
automations.next: Watch the daily digest. Accuracy on new leads is not measured beyond the 48-lead set.

automations.name: Inbox triage
automations.what: Sorts incoming email, marks anything time-sensitive and saves a reply as a Gmail draft that is never sent. Courts, other lawyers, spam and instruction-like text get no draft.
automations.evidence: 54 invented emails scored offline with stand-in models. A perfect model scores 54 of 54, and a failing or hostile model still passes the 49 guarantees the rules can check.
automations.limit: Only 10 invented emails have been through the real model, one at a time, so how well it sorts real email is not measured. Five gaps are listed in the project notes.
automations.next: Run the 54 invented emails through the live core for a real accuracy number.

automations.name: Consultation booking
automations.what: Offers free first-consultation times for a practice area and books the one a person picks, on the website or by voice. Rules choose the attorney and enforce notice, buffer, one booking per person and the conflict check. No AI model.
automations.evidence: 86 invented cases, 86 of 86. A separate brute-force check agrees on 72 scenarios across both daylight-saving changes (20,677 free times compared). 46 deliberate breakages of the rules were all caught.
automations.limit: Same-author labels. The double-booking check passed one live race of two requests. No email verification, holiday calendar or cancel endpoint yet; a kept booking adds a calendar entry.
automations.next: Add a holiday calendar and a way to cancel.

automations.name: Court-notice extraction
automations.what: A vision model copies a scanned court paper into fields and tested rules set the priority. Every result is saved as Needs attorney confirmation and nothing can approve one. Dates are repeated as printed and no deadline is ever worked out.
automations.evidence: 12 invented notices. A perfect reader reproduces 12 of 12 labels, 800 random readings agree with a separately written restatement of the rules, and 53 deliberate breakages of the rules were all caught.
automations.limit: No model has read the images yet. A model that calls every page not a court document would leave urgent notices without an alert (8 of 8 in the stand-in test). The images go to a third-party model, so only invented papers belong in the demo.
automations.next: Upload the 12 notices through the live form and score the saved rows.

automations.name: Voice line
automations.what: Answers questions about the firm by voice and books a first consultation through the same booking service as the website. Urgent wording, advice requests and changes get fixed replies, and a check blocks any answer that gives advice, states a deadline or invents a fee.
automations.evidence: 124 offline tests, including the booking dialog run against the real booking rules. 54 invented questions: the right knowledge reaches the model for all 43 that need it, and the 11 that must not go to the model do not.
automations.limit: The chat model's answers have not been measured, and nobody has tried it with a real microphone yet.
automations.next: Run the live question set and make one real call.

linksToday: The intake reply offers the booking page when the matter looks like one the firm handles.
The booking service accepts the intake reference, so a booking can be tied to the form that led to it.
The website form and the voice line book through the same two endpoints and the same rules.
A scanned court notice sends one alert to the attorney on duty, with no party names.

Intake, triage, booking and notices each write one short event per run to one shared log, with no names, addresses or message text. A daily digest and an error alert read it, and a nightly job deletes old log rows after 90 days. Running in n8n since 2026-11-12; a voice booking is logged by the booking workflow.
linksLater: A new-matter email from the triage inbox becoming an intake lead (today it is only labelled for the intake coordinator).
A court notice that arrives by email going straight to the notices workflow.
rules: No workflow sends a message to a client or a visitor on its own judgment. The one automatic email is the fixed booking confirmation, sent only to the address that booked.
A model can only add care. Time-sensitive wording, conflicts and the choice of attorney are decided by tested rules.
Nothing here says whether anyone has a case, what a deadline is, or what will happen. Replies carry that in plain words.
Court notices are never approved by a machine
Logs and alerts hold references and categories, not names, email addresses or message text.
